# Blackbox Protocol — Skill Notes

Canonical named competency roster. DESIGN-NOTES.md owns learning mechanics and design decisions; this file owns catalogue names and IDs. Publication introduction is not an era lock. Core is inherited by Signal Lost; both are inherited by Dead Zone. General access may require resources/prerequisites; occupational (Professional Learning Tree) access requires credible occupational or qualification gates. All entries have levels I–V. Core conditionally approved subject to occupation and gameplay coverage; expansion selections are working drafts. Exact names and IDs preserved from CCDD-16–18. Semantic overlap, prerequisites, complexity, assessment and occupation mapping remain pending. Ordinary hunting/trapping and wilderness first aid are placed in Signal Lost additions for now, but are learnable in Core campaigns; review whether to relocate to Core during coverage audit without changing totals. No mathematical changes.

| Publication | General | Occupational | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Core | 200 | 150 | 350 |
| Signal Lost additions | 35 | 15 | 50 |
| Dead Zone additions | 120 | 30 | 150 |
| Total | 355 | 195 | 550 |

## CDR eligibility (approved working rule)

Minimum character CDR is a non-spendable eligibility threshold checked before activating each sequential level. All other requirements remain mandatory. Award incremental CDR only after completion; never deduct it. Documented starting occupational history grants justified levels without retroactive threshold gating; personal purchases must meet thresholds using already validated grants and earlier eligible purchases, not the award from the target itself (implementation default pending review). Thresholds are provisional for playtesting. See DESIGN-NOTES.md CCDD-19 and MANUAL-CHARTS.md.

| 2 | 0 | 200 | 1000 | 3000 | 6000 |

## Universal competency modifier (CCDD-20)

User-approved competency modifier: B(L)=5×max(0,L−1), for integer L=0–5. Level I grants no D100 bonus but retains CDR, training and prerequisite value. Each level II–V adds +5 percentage points to the same competency's total (0/5/10/15/20 for I–V). Apply only the highest relevant competency total once per check; never sum separate competencies or previous level totals, never permanently increase underlying general skill. Final possible D100 target remains capped at 99. All other learning mechanics unchanged.

## Record conventions

Draft specification, not playtested. Governing skills and complexity use revised working assignments; remaining semantic and balance validation is pending. Complexity adjustments are provisional and use the unchanged CCDD formulas. Level I–V respectively fundamentals, basic practical, independent, advanced, mastery. Each level requires prior level, listed supporting prerequisites at I/I/II/III/IV respectively (unless stated otherwise), appropriate access, actual in-world hours, resources, practice and GM-approved assessment. No listed supporting prerequisite means none proposed, not exemption from access or safety. Professional access requires relevant institution, authorized training or documented equivalent; credentials and authority remain separate. CCDD-22 applies to every professional record, including inherited prerequisites: modern institutional names describe a discipline, not a mandatory historical institution. Native and transitional characters may meet the same gate through qualified local mentorship, supervised practice and documented assessment; no automatic levels, CDR or authority. General access is open or resource/prerequisite restricted. Level bonuses +0/+5/+10/+15/+20, highest applicable only. Numeric sequences below are in I–V order: incremental hours, cumulative creation point cost from unlearned, incremental CDR award, cumulative CDR. Upgrade creation cost is difference, not sum. CCDD-12 governs discounts, slots and progress. No clinical or other real-world authorization is conferred. Training hours are game defaults, not professional qualification durations. Assessment rubric is a proposed common rubric: I explain scope and limitations; II demonstrate a routine task with guidance; III independently complete representative task; IV resolve a complex scenario and justify decisions; V demonstrate repeatable expert performance and evaluate alternatives. For each record apply rubric to named discipline and listed resources; hazardous/regulated tasks use simulation or qualified supervision. Detailed discipline-specific assessment cases, mandatory credential hours and alternative routes remain pending.


## Core — General

### G-001 — Culinary fundamentals

Scope: Meal preparation; applies only to tasks within this discipline, not adjacent specialties or independent legal authority. Governing: Crafting (DEX). Complexity 2. Access: general; suitable resources. Supporting prerequisites: none proposed. Resources: kitchen, ingredients, utensils; resource verification: representative practice equipment, sufficient task-specific materials or consumables, and a safe practice setting; Equivalent accessible training resources may substitute only when they support the same assessment evidence. Assessment: produce a meal meeting stated quality, portion and safety criteria. Apply the common I–V rubric to increasing independence and complexity; record evidence and GM approval.

Assessment evidence (revised): finished sample and quality inspection. Assessment focus: Meal preparation. I — recognize acceptable and defective samples and material constraints for culinary fundamentals. II — produce a guided sample and record defects for culinary fundamentals. III — produce an independently accepted sample against quality and safety specifications for culinary fundamentals. IV — adapt production to a changed material or quality constraint and compare results for culinary fundamentals. V — produce two accepted samples under different constraints and explain defect prevention for culinary fundamentals. Apply any existing specific assessment requirement and the full scope boundary. Fail for unmet predefined acceptance criteria, unsupported evidence, critical safety or authorization breach, or assistance beyond the level allowance. Regulated and hazardous activities use qualified fictional supervision or simulation; no real-world qualification implied.

## Section 2 prerequisite and overlap review

Working revision: mandatory dependencies are reserved for foundational knowledge; recommended experience is not a gate. CCDD-22 access and assessment remain mandatory. All 550 dependency nodes checked for missing references and cycles. The following overlap boundaries guide applicability; never stack bonuses for the same task. No IDs retired in this pass.

| Competency A | Competency B | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| G-005 Food preservation | DZ-G-086 Salt curing and smoking | General preservation versus constrained-resource curing and smoking |
| G-200 Library and archive organization | DZ-G-074 Offline knowledge preservation | Collection organization versus durable offline preservation |
| SL-G-008 Hunting | DZ-G-105 Subsistence hunting | Individual lawful hunting versus sustained subsistence resource stewardship |
| SL-G-009 Trapping | DZ-G-106 Subsistence trapping | Individual lawful trapping versus sustained subsistence resource stewardship |
| G-131 Bookkeeping | DZ-G-066 Local exchange accounting | Ordinary bookkeeping versus noncurrency exchange records |
| G-034 Route planning | DZ-G-109 Overland expedition logistics | Route selection versus expedition sustainment |
| G-124 Conflict resolution | DZ-G-069 Community mediation | Interpersonal dispute resolution versus community mediation |
| DZ-G-069 Community mediation | DZ-G-117 Community dispute arbitration | Facilitated agreement versus formal arbitration and recorded decisions |
| DZ-G-030 Traditional rope making | DZ-G-094 Natural fiber cordage production | Finished rope assembly and inspection versus intermediate natural fiber cordage preparation; differentiated in subsequent scope revision |
| G-189 Continuity planning fundamentals | SL-G-035 Household continuity planning | Organizational continuity versus household continuity |
| G-101 First aid | SL-G-004 Wilderness first aid | Immediate first aid versus remote care constraints |
| P-054 Internal medicine | DZ-P-006 Austere clinical medicine | Clinical medicine versus constrained-resource clinical adaptation |
| G-129 Teaching fundamentals | P-138 Professional classroom instruction | General instruction versus professional classroom practice |

Subsequent review: title and scope inventory reviewed, additional overlap boundaries revised; occupation grants and assessment evidence remain subject to cross-system validation. No changes to global proficiency or progression formulas in this pass.


### Additional semantic boundary corrections

Revised 29 scope definitions across 15 overlap pairs. Retained existing competency IDs and progression tables; overlapping tasks do not stack competency bonuses. Assessment and resource alignment remain subject to subsequent review.


### Section 2 semantic review checkpoint

All 550 title/scope pairs inventoried; 550 unique IDs, titles and scope strings. Additional lexical similarity screening identified five high-similarity title pairs; road/off-road driving, database fundamentals/administration and routine/emergency public health scopes were clarified, while shelter and veterinary pairs already had explicit boundaries. Total revised scope definitions across the two passes: 35. No IDs or progression tables changed. This is a catalogue-level semantic review, not proof that all possible task scenarios are mutually exclusive. Assessment evidence, resources and occupation grant alignment are separate remaining checks.


### Assessment evidence revision checkpoint

Replaced 550 generic draft rubrics with 21 evidence-family progression patterns bound to each competency title and scope (2,750 level clauses). Each level requires observable evidence; mastery requires two contrasting accepted performances. GM defines case-specific measurable tolerances before assessment; critical safety and authorization failures cannot be offset by other performance. Existing specific assessments, access gates, prerequisites, resources and numeric progression remain unchanged. These are family-based rubrics, not 550 individually authored scenario banks; scenario-specific tolerances and playtesting remain necessary.


### Resource requirements validation checkpoint

All 550 resource records inspected for presence and revised with evidence-linked resource verification and publication-appropriate alternatives. Twenty-two shared clinical, aviation and industrial descriptions received additional discipline-specific materials. Before training begins, GM records required resource functions, available quantity or capacity, access duration, consumable replenishment, instructor/assessor availability, and any approved equivalent. Missing mandatory resources block affected training or assessment; no automatic waiver, bonus or advancement. Simulation is valid only where the assessment permits it and cannot establish real-world credentials. Dead Zone alternatives must preserve functional adequacy and safety, not assume electricity, network access or surviving institutions. Quantities and availability remain scenario-dependent; no universal item-price or stock assumptions added. Numeric progression unchanged.
